source.title: Armagh Guardian, 3 June 1927, p. 3 (list of the new county council: "Returned Unopposed" and "Retiring Councillors deemed to be re-elected"); nominations from the Newry Reporter, 28 April 1927, p. 6 ("County Elections: Nominations in Armagh")
source.publisher: Armagh Guardian (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: every name checked against the two page images; returned unopposed, no poll

note: Triennial election of the county council, 1927: nominations received by Thomas E. Reid, secretary, 26 April 1927; the only poll was in Portadown, 26 May 1927. No party labels are printed for the unopposed members in the nominations or the list of the new council, so none are given. Returned unopposed. Thomas Mallon: no party label printed in 1927. At other elections he stood as Nationalist (Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1923, printed 'Nationalists': Portadown News, 13 January 1923, p. 3 ("The Municipal Elections"); Armagh Guardian, 12 January 1923, p. 3 ("Keady"); Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1926, printed 'Nat.': Belfast News-Letter, 18 January 1926, p. 7 ("Big poll at Keady"); Keady, Keady Urban District, 15 January 1929, printed 'N.': Witness (Belfast), 18 January 1929, p. 8 ("Keady"); also the Irish Weekly and Ulster Examiner, 19 January 1929, p. 11, and the Armagh Guardian, 18 January 1929, p. 2).
